answer: Operator-Linked Revenue Clawback: each wallet routes a small share of fees to a shared operator pool tagged by cross-wallet graph clustering (shared funding, timing, co-located calls). Any cluster proven to be one operator forfeits the whole pool, and future pools carry that debit like a dune burying its base. Attackers must keep distinct funding rivers and timing to avoid clustering; each extra identity raises overhead and lowers the clawback edge. Honest operators see a stable ivory payout.
